text:
maya: heads-up — during a customer load test we saw per-key queues fill and the svc started returning a bunch of 503s. wants to align on policy: 429 vs 503, and where to do shedding (edge vs runtime).
juan: can you paste a brief timeline/logs?
omar: fyi the spike was ~3x normal RPS for 6 mins, most traffic was a few org keys.
maya: log snippet — timestamped error rates and queue depth:
```
2025-11-07T14:12:01Z INFO queue_depth=0
2025-11-07T14:13:22Z WARN queue_depth=1024 per_key_hotspot=org:acme
2025-11-07T14:14:05Z ERROR accept_fail=1 code=503 backend_timeout
```
oliver: hmm. two axes: 1) per-key rate limiting (429) 2) pre-queue global shedding (503) when runtime is overloaded.
sam: prefer 429 for per-key bursts, with Retry-After. 503 for degraded node-level failures where we can't meaningfully honor any requests.
lee: Agree. 429 lets clients backoff gracefully; but some customers treat 503 as transient and auto-retry which worsens the spike.
juan: question — do we want the edge LB to do early shedding or let the runtime reject? Edge can cheaply inspect keys and enforce token-bucket per-key. Runtime has better view of GPU/backpressure.
maya: proposed hybrid: per-key token buckets at edge (soft limits + short burst tokens), runtime enforces hard limits and returns 503 when CPU/GPU queue depth > threshold.
oliver: sketch of config we could add to platform config:
```yaml
rate_limit:
  per_key: 100 rps
  per_key_burst: 500 tokens
  global_queue_limit: 2000
  queue_shed_policy: '503-when-queue-above-threshold'
  retry_after_seconds: 2
```
sam: minor tweak: make per_key_burst time-windowed (token refill rate) and add per-org quotas for paid tiers. free-tier gets smaller bucket and stricter backoff suggestions.
maya: telemetry item list: per-key queue depth, per-key 429 rate, node-level 503 rate, end-to-end latency p95/p99, retry volume, and an alert when 503 spikes > 1% for 5m.
lee: we'll need a new dashboard tile in Console: "Shedding — 429 vs 503" with a stacked bar: 429 by org, 503 by node. Also link to runbook.
juan: on rollout — feature-flag the edge per-key limiter. Start with conservative per_key 50rps + 200 burst for 24h, monitor. If stable, expand.
oliver: also add headers to responses so clients can differentiate:
- 429 X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After
- 503 X-Server-Queue-Depth, X-Server-Instance

sam: we should update SDKs to surface Retry-After and backoff helpers. Quick PR in client-lib to add exponential backoff with Retry-After support.
maya: runbook decision? propose: implement hybrid shedding, default behavior: per-key -> 429; global overload -> 503. Add explicit doc on when to retry vs when to degrade.
lee: agree. Also add a temporary mitigation: auto-fallback to smaller model variants for orgs that hit sustained high per-key cost to reduce queue pressure.
juan: testing plan: synthetic per-key spike tests + chaos to induce node-level overload. Collect metrics and validate dashboards.
sre-bot: deploy scheduled: edge limiter gate (ff=u128) -> 2025-11-08 02:00 UTC canary to 5% of traffic.
maya: I'll file the tickets: 1) edge limiter impl + config 2) runtime queue-threshold enforcement + header 3) console dashboard 4) SDK update. Assigning: juan -> edge, oliver -> runtime, lee -> console, sam -> SDK.
sam: estimated effort: edge 2d, runtime 3d, console 1d, sdk 1d.
lee: add an alert to PagerDuty for 503 cluster-wide > 0.5% in 2m during rollout window.
juan: quick note — make sure per-key limits are bypassable via org-level override for enterprise (with audit log).
maya: thanks team. we'll discuss rollback criteria in the canary channel: if p50 latency + token cost per request increases by > 20% or 503 > 0.5% we rollback.
oliver: one more thought — for long tail requests with huge context, prefer rejecting early with 429 (client should trim context) rather than letting them queue.
maya: agreed. ok I'll push tickets and add sample configs + runbook snippets. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks!
